passage: In Aaji's house in the kasba, Hrithik squeezed behind the rice sacks in the storeroom. "Ready!" he called. Aaji Usha shuffled in, peering. "Is Hrithik under the cot? No. In the steel cupboard? No." Hrithik pressed both hands over his mouth, shoulders shaking. She walked right past the sacks. She doesn't know, he thought, eyes shining. When she turned away, he jumped out. "Boo! You didn't find me!" Aaji clutched her chest and laughed.

qa.q: Where did Hrithik hide?
qa.a: He squeezed behind the rice sacks in the storeroom.

qa.q: What does Hrithik pressing his hands over his mouth suggest?
qa.a: He was bursting with glee and trying hard not to give himself away, because he knew Aaji did not know where he was.

qa.q: How could Aaji keep this game fun and fair?
qa.a: She can keep pretending to search in several places and then let Hrithik take a turn as the seeker too.

qa.q: What might Aaji be enjoying in this game?
qa.a: She seems to enjoy playing along and hamming up her surprise, which makes her grandson's trick feel like a success. 😊

grounding: A small-town boy delights in hiding from his grandmother, knowing she cannot see where he is.

passage: On a Lisbon beach, Mateo hid a white pebble in one fist and put both hands behind his back. He shuffled them around. "Which hand, Beatriz?" His big sister tapped the left. He opened it, empty, and squealed. "You don't know! Only I know!" The next time, he pressed his lips tight and tried to keep a straight face, but his eyes kept sliding to his right hand. Beatriz smiled and chose right.

qa.q: What did Mateo hide in his fist?
qa.a: He hid a white pebble.

qa.q: Why was Mateo so thrilled when Beatriz picked the empty hand?
qa.a: He was delighted to realise that she didn't know something he knew, which made the trick feel powerful and fun.

qa.q: What could Mateo try next time to keep his secret better?
qa.a: He could practise keeping his eyes still, since his glances toward the right hand gave the pebble away. 🤔

qa.q: How does Beatriz seem to see the game?
qa.a: She seems amused and kind, playing along and reading his eyes, which shows she enjoys the game with him.

grounding: A young boy discovers that his sister cannot know which hand holds the pebble unless he shows her.

passage: At the preschool, Suraj Sir covered his eyes and counted. Keerthana tucked the class teddy inside the dress-up basket, then pressed a finger to her lips at her friends. "Shh! Don't tell." Suraj Sir looked under the mats and behind the curtain, muttering, "Where could Teddy be?" Keerthana bounced on her toes. "He doesn't know!" she whispered. When he finally opened the basket, she shrieked with laughter and begged, "Again! Now you close your eyes!"

qa.q: Where did Keerthana hide the class teddy?
qa.a: She tucked it inside the dress-up basket.

qa.q: How can you tell Keerthana felt delighted to know something the teacher didn't?
qa.a: She bounced on her toes, whispered "He doesn't know!" and shrieked with laughter when he found it.

qa.q: How could Suraj Sir extend this game for the class?
qa.a: He could let children take turns hiding the teddy and ask, "Who knows where it is, and who doesn't?"

qa.q: What would change if Suraj Sir had peeked while counting?
qa.a: The trick would be spoiled, and Keerthana would miss the fun of seeing that others don't know everything she knows.

grounding: A preschooler hides a teddy and relishes that her teacher does not know where it is.

passage: I'm Arnab's mama, and last Sunday I played hide-and-seek with him. The first time, he stood behind the curtain with his toes poking out, giggling loudly. Second time, he crouched behind the sofa and held both hands over his mouth. I walked past, saying, 'Where is he?' He waited, then leapt out. 'You didn't know!' He looked thrilled. Vaibhav, his dad, said Arnab asked to play it again at bedtime.

qa.q: Where did Arnab hide the second time?
qa.a: He crouched behind the sofa with both hands over his mouth.

qa.q: What does Arnab shouting 'You didn't know!' suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: He seemed delighted and proud that he had tricked his uncle, having found out that others do not know everything he knows.

qa.q: How could adults keep this kind of trick playful and safe?
qa.a: They can play along, act surprised and laugh with him, keeping it a game both sides enjoy.

qa.q: What might Vaibhav notice about his son from his bedtime request?
qa.a: He might see that Arnab loves this new game of fooling someone for fun, and is excited to try again.

grounding: Illustrates a child learning playful trickery through hide-and-seek, observed by his uncle.

passage:
First week: Kamal played hiding with Baljeet by covering his own eyes. 'I'm hiding!' Baljeet could see all of him.
Two weeks later, Kamal hid in the cupboard but shouted, 'I'm in the cupboard!'
A month on, he hid a marble in one fist, held out both hands to Baljeet and kept his face very still. 'Which hand?' Baljeet picked wrong. Kamal opened the other fist and burst out laughing.

qa.q: What did Kamal do in the first week to hide?
qa.a: He covered his own eyes and said 'I'm hiding!'

qa.q: Why did Kamal keep his face very still in the marble game?
qa.a: He wanted Baljeet not to guess, so he tried to hide what he knew behind a calm face.

qa.q: How could Baljeet support Kamal's game as it grows?
qa.a: He can take turns being the tricker, and laugh together when either one is fooled, so it stays friendly.

qa.q: How might the game feel different for Baljeet in the first week compared with a month later?
qa.a: In the first week it was easy and cute for him, but later he truly had to guess and could be fooled.

grounding: Shows a child gradually learning to play small tricks as he realises others cannot see what he knows.
